availability.expectation: Measure existing invocation success and outage intervals per action. No zero-downtime guarantee or universal maintenance-window requirement.
availability.drain: Never purge, cancel or delete workloads to force completion.

temporary_combinations.mixed_compute_fleet: Keep one source compute cluster and one target cluster at the mixed state. Verify original and new workloads, JWTs, credentials and registrations on both before advancing.

unsupported: physical GPU and cross-host failure qualification
recovery of nonempty NATS memory streams or undrained invocation, session and task state

preconditions: Umbrella source/target selections and all three stack identities are locked.
Required chart/image access and selected package/image inspection pass.
All route-specific execution blockers have explicit reviewed resolution.
postconditions: Release inventories match exact tags, source commits and digests.
Private three-way render diff preserves topology, identities and credentials.
Each endpoint matches its umbrella manifest or the frozen legacy baseline matrix.
Workload-created helpers and inline hook images have separate effective references, immutable digests and provenance checks, including entries absent from original inventories.
evidence: private effective configuration and render diff
actions.recovery: No application mutation. Fix access or configuration, then use a new run identity.

preconditions: Inventory action passed; source HA topology, both existing compute clusters at 1.0.0 and observability 1.0.0 are healthy.
postconditions: Existing HTTP, gRPC, secret-reading functions and a task pass; original identities and credentials are saved.
evidence: OpenBao cluster ID, mounts, JWKS and canary
actions.recovery: Do not start the hop. Retain the failed baseline and its private diagnostics.

preconditions: External callers are paused through an explicit operator checkpoint; every affected function/version and task is inventoried.
postconditions: No pending/in-flight invocations or running tasks remain before disruptive operations; timeouts retain workloads.
Affected source data writers remain paused through the final data gate and consistent backup; retain every original workload and terminal task record.
actions.recovery: Resume callers only after checking source health. Never purge queues or cancel tasks to satisfy drain.

preconditions: The source baseline, retained workload identities and installation history are recorded.
Source service image versions and actual migration-task availability are verified independently of Helm chart versions.
SIS 0.7.2 does not contain InstanceLookupBackfillTask. Compare every retained sis_api.instances row with its referenced request for deployment_id and gpu_specification_id before the hop.
postconditions: Source lookup comparisons report no conflicting fields, missing live requests or failed reads. Null legacy fields that need repair block this exact route until a reviewed migration procedure exists.
Verify backfill availability in the actual target SIS 0.7.7 image. Any target repair requires an explicit during-hop boundary and does not replace source prerequisites.

Every retained instance that requires target lookup has matching non-null IDs in the instance and authoritative request. Two null values do not satisfy a required lookup; record independent null counts and any reviewed terminal exclusions.
evidence: source service tag and runtime image digest
private lookup comparison or final VALIDATE summary with all counters
task mode, pod UID, scan timestamps and affected-writer pause record
independent required-lookup null counts and authoritative request comparison
actions.recovery: Stop before backup or the hop on incomplete, stale, null or conflicting lookup evidence. Preserve source row and workload identities. This source has no lookup backfill task; the migration owner must define any required repair. A successful schema Job does not replace this data check.

preconditions: The source is healthy; writers can be quiesced for a consistent snapshot without deleting or canceling workloads.

The declared drained-memory-cold-restore profile applies: all native stream messages/bytes and consumer pending/acknowledgement/redelivery counts are zero in two stable observations after the caller/writer pause.
A complete frozen stream and durable-consumer inventory matches both observations. Unknown streams, changed configurations, nonterminal tasks or nonempty state block this profile.
postconditions: Cassandra data/schema, NATS streams/configuration, OpenBao Raft and Kubernetes configuration restore successfully in isolated storage.

The isolated full-stack restore preserves stream and consumer names/configurations, original storage/replication, workload IDs, registrations and credentials. Native memory sequence/cursor resets are recorded explicitly; original/new application behavior passes with no lost pending work because the captured cohort was drained.
evidence: per-stream storage, replicas, configuration, messages and consumer-state inventory
drained-memory checkpoint and isolated full-stack recovery proof
actions.recovery: Keep the source unchanged. Resolve backup or restore failures before proceeding.

preconditions: Recorded source and target compute inventories, exact artifacts and effective values are verified.
Pause/drain, consistent restore and applicable control-plane/JWT prerequisites passed.
The candidate temporary combinations are reviewed for this exact control plane; admission and hostname policies required by the selected packages are satisfied.
postconditions: Each existing compute cluster advances from 1.0.0 to 1.0.5 without re-registration, identity loss or topology changes.
After the first cluster update, original and new function/task invocations and secret injection pass on both source and target compute clusters.
Final invocations and deployments pass on both target compute clusters before advancing.
evidence: per-cluster source/target runtime digests and revisions
mixed-fleet original/new HTTP and gRPC invocation results
task and secret-injection results on both cluster versions
actions.recovery: Stop on the first failure and retain partial fleet state. Revalidate current postconditions before resuming. Do not re-register clusters or blindly replay uncertain operations; use the tested recovery boundary.

preconditions: Pause/drain and tested restore gates passed.
Exact migration images and their schemas are reviewed.
OpenBao/JWT and NATS transition ordering is verified against selected packages before mutation.
postconditions: Cassandra source records, clean ledgers and RF/DC are preserved.
NATS streams, consumers, identities and replication remain valid.
No core consumer rollout starts before the applicable data postconditions pass.
evidence: Job UID and exact image digest
HA quorum and original topology snapshot
actions.recovery: Stop consumers and retain evidence on unknown migration outcome. Restore the consistent backup after a data boundary; Helm rollback alone is insufficient.

preconditions: Selected chart hook order and migration-helper interactions are reviewed.
Source catalog SHA, plugin bytes, mounts, credentials and Raft recovery material are recorded.
postconditions: Existing mounts and old/new JWT canaries pass without catalog SHA rewriting.
Target migration data postconditions pass and all HA members preserve the original cluster identity.
actions.recovery: Stop rotation on failed quorum or canary. Do not initialize a new cluster. Use the tested Raft restore procedure when required.

preconditions: Migration postconditions and OpenBao canaries pass before new consumers start.
Source lookup prerequisites passed before backup; target schema Job completion does not replace service-level data checks.
postconditions: Core and remaining enabled control-plane stages become ready without changing HA topology or identities.
Original and new workloads work against compute 1.0.5 before the next action.

Target SIS 0.7.7 passes matching lookup validation with zero missing live requests, mismatches and failures. Verify actual task availability before using VALIDATE. Any target repair requires its own recovery boundary.
evidence: target SIS backfill task mode and final VALIDATE counters
actions.recovery: Stop further rollouts. Determine whether data remains backward compatible before restoring binaries; otherwise restore the consistent backup.

preconditions: All preceding actions have current matching evidence.
postconditions: Original and new function/task invocations work on both target compute clusters.
Credentials, registrations, workload IDs and durable data are preserved.
Final control/compute/observability versions match the locked endpoint.
Mixed-fleet checkpoints, availability and hands-on effort are recorded; callers resume only after acceptance.
evidence: original/new HTTP and gRPC canary results
actions.recovery: Do not resume production callers or claim qualification on a failed acceptance. Follow the tested recovery boundary.

configuration_checks: Three-way merge source defaults, source site values and target defaults; retain secrets without putting them in reports.
Keep the source service replica counts, Cassandra RF/DC, NATS stream replicas, storage and placement. Do not select target HA defaults that silently resize existing services.
Retain upstream or mirrored cert-manager repository overrides; these images do not inherit global.image.
Do not reuse source chart/image pins as site overrides; verify every effective pin against the selected inventory.
Use exact selected chart packages rather than current source defaults. Record differences between packaged defaults, inventory references and stack source.

Resolve umbrella endpoints through their pinned released manifests. Verify each selected stack tag, source commit and inventory digest. Version 1.0.1 uses its frozen legacy matrix without a synthetic manifest.
Select source and target peer versions from their separate recorded matrices. Preserve registration files, credentials and topology while changing the selected compute/observability releases.
migration_checks: Compare actual Cassandra migration images, SQL trees and upgrade tasks for these umbrella selections. Preserve clean ledgers, source data and RF/DC mappings.
Check source installation history and service backfill availability before target rollout. Missing source tasks require an explicit bridge or blocker, not inferred completion.
Compare selected OpenBao hooks, migration helpers and JWT plugin lifecycle. Preserve Raft identity, catalog entries, mounts and old/new JWT behavior.
Review NATS persistence, stream and consumer configuration, and reloader behavior for the exact source/target artifacts. A higher umbrella version does not prove forward component selection.
Review cert-manager CRDs, webhook behavior, certificates and retained fixes against actual source/target selections.
Recheck historical init SQL and explicit upgrade migrations independently. Do not replay old init files or infer data backfills from Job completion.

comparison_scope.peer_selection: Use released umbrella manifests. Use the frozen legacy matrix only for baseline 1.0.1.
comparison_scope.mixed_compute_fleet: Candidate states requiring independent live acceptance; no supported execution is enabled.

execution_blockers: The umbrella scope changes the control-plane endpoint to stack 1.0.10. Recheck action ordering, effective configuration, migration/runtime behavior and recovery for these exact inputs. Prior stack 1.0.4 rehearsals do not satisfy this gate.
Before supported execution, bind enabled-profile artifact coverage and migration/runtime acceptance to the exact artifacts, configuration, topology and current run.

Require matching HA preservation, mixed-fleet, consistent restore and end-to-end workload evidence for the intended profile. Scoped laboratory acceptance does not qualify broader configurations or failure recovery.
Require native NATS stream/consumer configuration, storage-permission and replication checks across the repository change. Equal server binaries do not establish whole-image identity.
Before backup or any hop action, require source-data-prerequisites with zero missing live requests, mismatches or failures; preserve the validated data epoch through the backup.
Require original-reference identity for legacy NVCT helpers omitted from the source inventory before supported execution. Diagnostic repository access does not establish original byte equivalence.

For drained-memory-cold-restore, require matching paused-source observations and consistent isolated full-cohort restore acceptance. Nonempty or in-flight memory recovery remains unsupported; an earlier restore does not establish recovery from a later migration failure.

matrix_references.interpretation: All three endpoint stacks match the released umbrella manifest, except legacy baseline 1.0.1. Final versions do not qualify temporary or mixed-fleet states.

runtime_artifact_checks: Resolve function/task launch helpers and inline receipt-hook images from effective configuration and live Pod specifications. An absent inventory entry does not establish runtime absence.

Stack 1.0.1 NVCT remote configuration selects nvcf_worker_init:2.107.0, nvcf_worker_task:2.107.0 and ess-agent:1.1.0, omitted from its NVCT inventory entries. Original-reference access and actual payload identity require separate checks.

recovery_profile.scope: Caller-paused, fully drained function/task cohort with every selected memory stream empty and no consumer pending, acknowledgement or redelivery state.
recovery_profile.native_counter_reset: Cold restore resets memory stream sequences and consumer delivery/ack counters. This is accepted only for the verified drained cohort; durable names, full configurations, storage, replicas, application identities and persistent data must survive.
required_evidence: two stable complete native observations after the caller/writer pause, bound to the frozen stream/consumer inventory
no native task in a nonterminal state and no outstanding invocation or session lookup state
isolated full-stack restore using new storage, original Kubernetes trust material, registrations and credentials
original and new HTTP, gRPC, secret-injection and task acceptance after restore
unsupported: in-flight invocation, asynchronous result, session or task recovery
purging, cancellation, manual consumer reset or message replay to obtain a passing drain
